languageModelTools.name: jira_getTicket
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetches a Jira ticket's fields and description by key. Use to look up ticket details before answering a question or deciding what to change.
languageModelTools.userDescription: View a Jira ticket's fields and description.

languageModelTools.name: jira_searchTickets
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches Jira tickets using JQL (Jira Query Language) and returns a table of matching tickets.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search Jira tickets with a JQL query.

jql.description: JQL query, e.g. 'project = PROJ AND status = "In Progress"'

languageModelTools.name: jira_getComments
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetches the comments on a Jira ticket, most recent first.
languageModelTools.userDescription: View comments on a Jira ticket.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of comments to return (default 20).

languageModelTools.name: jira_listTemplates
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the ticket templates defined in this workspace's .jira-templates.json, each with its name and issue type. Call this before jira_createTicket to see whether a suitable template exists — a template carries default field values a bare issue type does not. Returns an empty list, not an error, when no templates file exists.
languageModelTools.userDescription: List the Jira ticket templates configured for this workspace.

languageModelTools.name: jira_discoverWorkflow
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Discovers and caches the Jira status-transition graph for a project/issue type by sampling real tickets in each status. Run this when jira_transitionTicket reports no direct transition to the target status, then retry the transition — it enables multi-hop transitions.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Sample a project's Jira workflow and cache its status transitions.

issueType.description: Issue type name, e.g. Bug, Story, Task

languageModelTools.name: jira_addComment
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds a comment to a Jira ticket. This writes to Jira — the user is asked to confirm the exact comment text before it is posted.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a comment to a Jira ticket.

comment.description: The comment text to post, in Jira wiki markup or plain text.

languageModelTools.name: jira_updateField
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Updates a single field on one Jira ticket. Supported field names: summary, description, priority, assignee, labels, components, fix version. This writes to Jira — the user is shown the current and new value and asked to confirm before it is written.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Update one field on a Jira ticket.

fieldName.description: Field to update: summary, description, priority, assignee, labels, components, or fix version.

value.description: New value. For labels/components, a comma-separated list.

languageModelTools.name: jira_createTicket
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Creates one new Jira ticket. Call jira_listTemplates first and prefer passing templateName over a bare issueType, since a template carries the process's default field values. If neither issueType nor a resolvable templateName is given, no ticket is created — the tool instead returns the project's valid issue types to choose from. This writes to Jira — the user is asked to confirm the project, issue type, and summary before the ticket is created.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Create a new Jira ticket, optionally from a template.

issueType.description: Issue type name, e.g. Bug, Story, Task. Prefer templateName when a suitable template exists — omit this when passing templateName and letting the template supply it.

templateName.description: Name of a template returned by jira_listTemplates. Preferred over a bare issueType.

languageModelTools.name: jira_transitionTicket
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Moves a Jira ticket to a target status, via a direct transition or a cached multi-hop workflow path (see jira_discoverWorkflow). This writes to Jira — the user is asked to confirm the ticket and target status before it is transitioned.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Move a Jira ticket to a new status.

targetStatus.description: Target status name, e.g. Done, In Progress

resolution.description: Resolution to set when transitioning to a closed state, e.g. Fixed, Won't Do

languageModelTools.name: bitbucket_getPullRequest
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetches a Bitbucket pull request's title, description, author, target branch, and source commit hash.
languageModelTools.userDescription: View a Bitbucket pull request's details.

project.description: Bitbucket project key (Data Center) or workspace (Cloud), e.g. PROJ or myworkspace

languageModelTools.name: bitbucket_getPullRequestDiff
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetches the unified diff for a Bitbucket pull request.
languageModelTools.userDescription: View a Bitbucket pull request's diff.

project.description: Bitbucket project key (Data Center) or workspace (Cloud), e.g. PROJ or myworkspace

contextLines.description: Diff context lines to request around each hunk (default: the configured ticketSidekick.bitbucket.reviewContextLines, 12).

languageModelTools.name: bitbucket_postComment
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Posts a comment to a Bitbucket pull request's activity feed. This writes to Bitbucket — the user is asked to confirm the exact comment text before it is posted.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Post a comment on a Bitbucket pull request.

project.description: Bitbucket project key (Data Center) or workspace (Cloud), e.g. PROJ or myworkspace

comment.description: The comment text to post to the pull request's activity feed.

ticketSidekick.jira.baseUrl.description: Base URL of your Jira instance (e.g. https://jira.mycompany.com)

ticketSidekick.jira.authType.description: Jira authentication mode: 'datacenter' uses Bearer PAT, 'cloud' uses Basic email:Atlassian-apiToken

ticketSidekick.jira.defaultProject.description: Default Jira project key (e.g. 'PROJ'). Used when creating tickets if no project is specified in your prompt.

ticketSidekick.jira.sprintBoardId.description: Jira Agile board ID to use for sprint lookups. Only needed if your project has multiple Scrum boards and the wrong one is selected automatically. Find the board ID in the URL — modern Jira: .../jira/software/projects/PROJ/boards/12345 — Data Center RapidBoard: .../jira/secure/RapidBoard.jspa?rapidView=12345 (use the rapidView value).

ticketSidekick.jira.requiredFields.description: Jira field names that must be set for ticket validation (e.g. ["assignee", "priority"])

ticketSidekick.jira.showConnectionInfo.description: When enabled, each @jira response starts with an italic line showing the active base URL, API version, and auth type.

ticketSidekick.jira.additionalDisplayFie.description: Field IDs always shown in @jira show output even when their value is null. Use @jira show fields on PROJ-123 to discover field IDs (e.g. ["customfield_10020", "customfield_10500"]).

ticketSidekick.jira.searchFields.description: Field IDs to add as extra columns in @jira search results (e.g. ["priority", "customfield_10020"]). Use @jira show fields on PROJ-123 to discover field IDs.

ticketSidekick.jira.hiddenDisplayFields.description: Field IDs excluded from @jira show output. Fields in additionalDisplayFields override this list. Use @jira show fields on PROJ-123 to discover field IDs.

ticketSidekick.jira.myTeamJql.description: JQL fragment representing your team's tickets (e.g. 'project = BACKEND AND assignee in membersOf("backend-team")'). When you ask '@jira open tickets for my team', this is ANDed with the rest of your query.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.baseUrl.description: Base URL of your Bitbucket Data Center instance (e.g. https://bitbucket.mycompany.com). Leave empty for Bitbucket Cloud.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.authType.description: Bitbucket authentication mode: 'datacenter' uses Bearer PAT, 'cloud' uses Basic base64(username:App-password)

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.showConnectionI.description: When enabled, each @bitbucket response (except check) starts with an italic line showing the active base URL, API version, and auth type.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.reviewInstructi.description: Additional instructions appended to the built-in PR review prompt. Use this to add project-specific guidance, e.g. 'This project follows Google Style Guide' or 'Focus on security issues only'. The built-in grounding rules and output format are always included.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.modelContextTok.description: Override the model's context window size in tokens for chunk sizing. Leave unset to use the model's reported value (recommended). Set this if auto-detection is unavailable or you want a conservative cap (e.g. 60000).

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.contextBudgetRa.description: Fraction of the model's context window to use per review chunk (0.1–0.9, default 0.7). The remaining 30% is reserved for the model's output. Lower this value if you see context-limit errors during reviews.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.reviewMode.description: Default review depth. 'standard' enables the two-pass review where the LLM can request additional file context. 'quick' skips the second pass (diffs only) — faster and cheaper for large PRs. Override per-review with '@bitbucket review quick <url>' or '@bitbucket review deep <url>'.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.reviewExcludePa.description: Glob patterns for files to skip during PR review (e.g. ["**/migrations/**", "**/*.snap", "**/*.generated.ts"]). Excluded files are not sent to the LLM; the review output notes how many were skipped.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.reviewContextLi.description: Number of unchanged context lines requested around each diff hunk (default 12). Wider context usually includes the enclosing function so the reviewer reasons about real surrounding code instead of guessing — at the cost of a larger prompt. Lower it to save tokens on large PRs.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.confidenceThres.description: Findings whose model-rated confidence falls below this value (0–1, default 0.7) are moved into a collapsed 'low-confidence' section rather than shown as primary findings. They are never discarded.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.detailedDiagnos.description: When enabled, each review additionally emits a single fenced structured run record to the "Ticket Sidekick" output channel — run configuration, per-call records, and the findings funnel with drop reasons — copy-pasteable as one block for comparing runs or filing a provider bug report.

ticketSidekick.email.deleteEmlAfterImpor.description: Delete the .eml file automatically after the Jira ticket is created.

ticketSidekick.veracode.minSeverity.description: Minimum Veracode severity (0=Informational … 5=Very High) to include when importing a Detailed Report. Flaws below this are filtered out by default (still visible in the raw XML).

ticketSidekick.veracode.includeRemediati.description: Veracode remediation_status values to include when importing a Detailed Report (e.g. exclude 'Fixed' or 'Mitigated'). Valid values: Cannot Reproduce, Fixed, Mitigated, New, Open, Potential False Positive, Remediated by User, Reopened, Reviewed - No Action Taken.

ticketSidekick.waltz.minVulnRating.description: Minimum 'Max Vuln Rating' to include when importing an OSS report. Components rated below this are filtered out by default (still visible in the raw file).

ticketSidekick.waltz.includeRemediationA.description: Remediation Action values to include when importing an OSS report (empty string means the column was blank). Components with any other action (e.g. 'Risk capture') are excluded by default.

walkthroughs.title: Ticket Sidekick: Jira
walkthroughs.description: Set up @jira and create your first ticket.

steps.title: Set your Jira base URL
steps.description:
Point Ticket Sidekick at your Jira instance.
[Open setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22ticketSidekick.jira.baseUrl%22)

steps.title: Add your Jira credentials
steps.description:
Store a Data Center Personal Access Token or Cloud email + API token in VS Code's encrypted Secret Storage.
[Set Data Center Token](command:ticket-sidekick.setDataCenterToken)
[Configure Cloud Credentials](command:ticket-sidekick.configureCloud)

steps.title: Set a default project
steps.description:
So `@jira create` and the report importers don't need a project key in every prompt.
[Open setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22ticketSidekick.jira.defaultProject%22)

steps.title: Discover your ticket types & workflow
steps.description:
Sample your project's real tickets to learn its issue types and status-transition graph.
[Ask @jira](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%5B%7B%22query%22%3A%22%40jira%20discover%20workflow%20%3CPROJECT%3E%20%3CISSUE_TYPE%3E%22%2C%22isPartialQuery%22%3Atrue%7D%5D)

steps.title: Create your first ticket
steps.description:
Generate a template from real project data, then create a ticket from it — or create one directly.
[Ask @jira](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%5B%7B%22query%22%3A%22%40jira%20generate%20a%20template%22%7D%5D)
[Or create directly](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%5B%7B%22query%22%3A%22%40jira%20create%20%3CTYPE%3E%20in%20%3CPROJECT%3E%3A%20%3CSUMMARY%3E%22%2C%22isPartialQuery%22%3Atrue%7D%5D)

walkthroughs.title: Ticket Sidekick: Bitbucket
walkthroughs.description: Set up @bitbucket and review your first pull request.

steps.title: Set your Bitbucket base URL (Data Center only)
steps.description:
Point Ticket Sidekick at your Bitbucket Data Center instance. Skip this on Bitbucket Cloud — Cloud always talks to the fixed api.bitbucket.org host.
[Open setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22ticketSidekick.bitbucket.baseUrl%22)

steps.title: Add your Bitbucket credentials
steps.description:
Store a Data Center Personal Access Token or Cloud username + App Password in VS Code's encrypted Secret Storage.
[Set Data Center Token](command:ticket-sidekick.setBitbucketDataCenterToken)
[Configure Cloud Credentials](command:ticket-sidekick.configureBitbucketCloud)

steps.title: Review your first pull request
steps.description:
Paste a real Bitbucket PR URL to @bitbucket and get a structured, line-accurate review.
[Ask @bitbucket](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%5B%7B%22query%22%3A%22%40bitbucket%20check%22%7D%5D)
[Review a PR](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%5B%7B%22query%22%3A%22%40bitbucket%20%3CURL%3E%22%2C%22isPartialQuery%22%3Atrue%7D%5D)
